_comment: planning.preflight.CATALOG (SDD §9.3): each finding code's severity, the strategies it concerns and its default remediation; a finding may give its own remediation or severity, as the API's finding() allows (MAP_NETWORK_MISSING's mapping target, NET_PORT_NOT_PERMITTED by policy profile, MAP_FLAVOR_*, MAP_VOLUME_TYPE_MISSING, MAP_GPU_FLAVOR's warning). test_preflight.py holds the API's catalog equal to it, and dashboard/src/api/findingCatalog.test.ts the offline mock's FINDING_CATALOG, which the mock's pre-flight reads.

SRC_VM_ERROR_STATE.remediation: Repair or reset the source VM (running or stopped), then re-validate.

SRC_VM_TRANSITIONAL_STATE.remediation: Wait until the Nova task finishes and the VM is ACTIVE or SHUTOFF, then re-validate.

SRC_VM_VOLUME_DETACHED.remediation: Attach the volume(s) to the source VM again, then re-validate: an earlier cutover attempt's export may have left them detached, and the migration never drops a disk the VM had at a cutover attempt. To migrate the VM without one, cancel the migration and plan the VM anew.

SRC_VM_DUPLICATE_NAME.remediation: Rename one of the VMs (os-migrate selects workloads by name) or migrate them in separate plans.

SRC_VM_NAME_UNUSABLE.remediation: Rename the VM in vCenter so that its name holds a Latin letter or a digit, then re-validate: the migration kit names the VM's server, ports and volumes after it.

SRC_VM_MULTIATTACH.remediation: Detach the shared volume before cutover or migrate the VM cold.

SRC_VM_EPHEMERAL_ROOT.remediation: The image-booted root disk is pre-copied through server snapshots (boot_disk_copy), which makes passes slower.

SRC_VM_HEAT_STACK.remediation: Seamless moves the server, not its stack: run no stack update at the source until the VM is finalized - an update may recreate the server - and follow the runbook for Heat stacks for the stack's other resources.

SRC_VM_AUTOSCALED.remediation: Suspend the group's scaling at the source - its scaling policies' alarms - as the runbook for Heat stacks says, then acknowledge the finding for the VM in the plan (acknowledged_findings) and re-validate.

SRC_VM_HEAT_UNKNOWN.remediation: Give the source credential a role Heat's policy lets list the project's stacks and their resources, or check with the runbook for Heat stacks whether the VM belongs to a stack or an autoscaling group: an autoscaling group may replace the server once the cutover stops it.

SRC_VM_LB_MEMBER.remediation: Move the membership as the runbook for Octavia load balancers says: drain the source member before the cutover, and add the migrated server to a pool at the destination once it is verified.

MAP_LB_POOL_INCOMPATIBLE.remediation: Map the source pool to a pool of a load balancer whose provider serves what the pool uses - an amphora one for HTTP, TLS termination or session persistence -, or accept that the clients reach the VM through an L4 pool after the cutover.

SRC_VM_LB_UNKNOWN.remediation: Give the source credential a role Octavia's policy lets list the project's pools and their members, or check the VM's memberships yourself with the runbook for Octavia load balancers.

MAP_NETWORK_MISSING.remediation: Add a network mapping or create a same-named network on the destination.

MAP_NETWORK_PRESTAGED.remediation: Nothing to do: pre-staging creates the network on the destination with the same name. Add a network mapping to use an existing destination network instead.

MAP_FLAVOR_PRESTAGED.remediation: Nothing to do: pre-staging creates the flavor on the destination with the same name, size and extra specs. Add a flavor mapping to use an existing destination flavor instead.

DST_KEYPAIR_MISSING.remediation: Create the keypair (its public key) for the destination's migration user, or pre-stage keypairs when the source migration user owns it.

MAP_KEYPAIR_PRESTAGED.remediation: Nothing to do: pre-staging imports the keypair (name and public key) for the destination's migration user.

MAP_FLAVOR_MISSING.remediation: Add a flavor mapping or create a destination flavor with enough vCPUs, RAM and root disk.

MAP_FLAVOR_AUTO.remediation: Add an explicit flavor mapping to override the automatically matched flavor.

MAP_VOLUME_TYPE_MISSING.remediation: Add a volume type mapping; otherwise the destination default volume type is used.

DST_QUOTA_INSUFFICIENT.remediation: Raise the destination project quotas or split the plan.

DST_PROJECT_MISSING.remediation: Map the VM's project to a project the destination lists (plan.mappings.projects): for a plan with a destination project, to the project its destination_project names, where its VMs land - or name in destination_project the project the VMs go to.

NET_MTU_SHRINK.remediation: Lower the guest MTU or map to a destination network with a larger MTU (ML2/OVN Geneve networks typically use 1442).

NET_SRIOV_PORT.remediation: SR-IOV/macvtap ports need an equivalent physnet on the destination; map the network accordingly.

NET_PORT_IPS.remediation: Turn on "Keep MAC addresses and every fixed IP" in the plan (port_creation_mode "neutron"), give each such port exactly one fixed IP before the cutover, or migrate the VM by storage handover when its ports have at most one address each.

MAP_NETWORK_AMBIGUOUS.remediation: Send the NIC to a name one destination network carries: one of the credential's project, or the only one of that name - map its network to such a name, or rename one of the networks.

NET_ADDRESS_REFUSED.remediation: Give the NIC an address its destination network takes: map its network to one whose subnets hold it, or set the address in a NIC override; for a SLAAC address keep the MAC (port_creation_mode "neutron").

NET_PORT_NOT_PERMITTED.remediation: Send the NIC to a network of the credential's project: map its network to one, or set a NIC override on the VM's migration page. Another project's shared network takes it once the destination credential has the role its policy profile counts: service under secure-RBAC, advsvc under the legacy rules. An external network that is not shared needs the admin role: Nova attaches it for no other.

MAP_NIC_OVERRIDE_INVALID.remediation: Fix the VM's network overrides on its migration page: an existing destination network, addresses inside its subnets, each given once in the plan. VMware VMs take none.

MAP_NIC_OVERRIDE.remediation: Nothing to do: each NIC goes where its override says.

VM_PCI_PASSTHROUGH.remediation: Map the VM's passthrough device in its plan to a GPU flavor of the destination: a GPU mapping of its PCI ids (VMware) or a flavor mapping (OpenStack). A device without ids cannot be mapped.

VM_VGPU.remediation: Map the VM's vGPU in its plan to a GPU flavor of the destination: a GPU mapping of its profile (VMware) or a flavor mapping (OpenStack).

MAP_GPU_FLAVOR.remediation: Check the GPU flavor's size and GPU before the cutover: GPU migration is a Technology Preview.

MAP_GPU_DOWNSIZED.remediation: Map the VM to a GPU flavor of the destination that gives at least the GPU it has, or confirm that its workload fits the smaller one.

DST_GPU_CAPACITY_INSUFFICIENT.remediation: Free GPU capacity in the destination, or move some of the plan's GPU VMs to a later plan or to another GPU flavor's pool, then re-validate.

DST_GPU_CAPACITY_UNKNOWN.remediation: Give the destination credential a role Placement lets read its allocation candidates (admin by default), or check the destination's GPU capacity yourself; a PCI alias's devices are configured in nova.conf.

GUEST_GPU_DRIVER.remediation: Install the NVIDIA driver the destination needs in the guest - a vGPU guest driver its vGPU manager supports, or the data center driver for a passed-through GPU - and test it after the cutover.

GUEST_GPU_LICENSE.remediation: Make the NVIDIA License System (a CLS instance or an on-premises DLS instance) reachable from the VM's destination network, and check the guest's license after the cutover.

VOL_ENCRYPTED.remediation: The Barbican key must be re-created on the destination before the volume can be attached.

GUEST_OS_LEGACY.remediation: Out of vendor support: it still migrates; test the application on the destination, check the virtio drivers and plan a longer verification.

GUEST_OS_UNKNOWN.remediation: Set the os_distro and os_version image properties (OpenStack) or run VMware Tools so the guest can be identified; verification uses the Linux profile meanwhile.

GUEST_CONVERSION_UNVERIFIED.remediation: virt-v2v converts this guest but Red Hat does not support the conversion: run a test conversion of a copy first.

GUEST_CONVERSION_UNSUPPORTED.remediation: The RHEL 9 conversion host has no drivers for this guest: install the virtio storage and network drivers from an older virtio-win release inside the guest and test the conversion, or migrate the VM another way.

VMW_CBT_DISABLED.remediation: Enable Changed Block Tracking on the VM or accept a cold migration.

VMW_INDEPENDENT_DISK.remediation: Independent disks are excluded from snapshots; change the disk mode or migrate cold.

VMW_SNAPSHOTS_PRESENT.remediation: Consolidate or delete the VM snapshots before migrating.

VMW_TOOLS_MISSING.remediation: Install or start VMware Tools for graceful shutdown and IP discovery.

DST_CAPABILITY_MISSING.remediation: Use a destination whose APIs provide the capability (SDD §21.4); upgrading the destination's services raises their maxima.

DST_RELEASE_OUTSIDE_SUPPORT.remediation: Prefer a Tier 1 series for production (SDD §21.1); declare the destination's series on the provider when its APIs cannot tell it, and run the destination lab matrix (QASuite §7.1) before relying on it.

CONV_HOST_MISSING.remediation: Configure a conversion host on the provider.

CONV_HOST_KEY_UNKNOWN.remediation: Declare the conversion host's public keys on its provider (conversion_host.ssh_host_keys), read out of band; or, for a host Seamless manages, delete it and pre-stage again, which creates it with an injected key.

CONV_HOST_KEYS_UNCHECKED.remediation: Set SEAMLESS_ANSIBLE_HOST_KEY_CHECKING to true: each conversion host then needs declared keys or a pin, which a host Seamless creates gets injected and the provider check reads from the console of one it finds.

HANDOVER_BACKEND_UNMAPPED.remediation: Map the volume type to a Cinder backend of the destination in handover.backend_map.

APP_PROBE_MISSING.remediation: Add an application probe for its service to the plan, for every VM or for this one (probe_overrides), or use the suggested probe on the plan page.

SRC_PORT_ADDRESS_PAIRS.remediation: Add the address pairs to the migrated server's ports at the destination once it is created (openstack port set --allowed-address), and check that the peers sharing an address - a keepalived pair's other member - reach it there.

MAP_FIP_ADDRESS_CHANGE.remediation: To keep an address, have the destination credential's project hold a floating IP of that address, with no port, before the cutover (an admin can create one with a given address on the external network); else update the clients, allowlists and DNS records of the old address after it.

DST_DNS_INTEGRATION_MISSING.remediation: Enable Neutron's DNS integration at the destination (an extension driver with Designate as its external DNS driver) and create the domain's zone for the destination credential's project, or publish the migrated VM's names in DNS yourself after the cutover.

NET_PREFIX_SPLIT.remediation: Put the VMs of each announced network into one wave, or have the network's prefix routed by hand while its waves are cut over.

NET_LB_POOL_SPLIT.remediation: Put each pool's members into one wave: give them one app tag and plan the waves again, as VMs that share an app tag stay together. Or accept that between its waves the pool serves from both clouds: its members already cut over are drained from the source pool and join the destination pool once verified - by the member helper for a pool the plan maps, else as the runbook for Octavia load balancers says.

DST_FIP_ADDRESS_UNAVAILABLE.remediation: Keep only addresses the destination can hold: an address of a subnet of its external network, free there or held detached by the destination credential's project, a token with a role that may choose a floating IP's address, and the quota for them - or let the plan take new addresses (network_cutover.floating_ips "auto").

NET_DNS_TTL_LONG.remediation: Lower the record's TTL below the plan's downtime SLO well before the window - a pre_stop hook may do it - or accept that clients keep the old address until the TTL runs out.

CEPH_ACCESS_MISSING.remediation: Give the source provider its Ceph access (ceph: fsid, monitors, client) and its key (PUT /providers/{id}/ceph-key), and run its check so that an rbd pool of that fsid is known; or turn extent_tracking off. Every pass scans in full until then.

EXTENT_TRACKING_PARTIAL.remediation: Nothing stops the migration: the named disks scan in full on every pass, the others use their extents. A tracked disk is an unencrypted Cinder RBD volume of the source's cluster whose host the source credential can read.

EXTENT_TRACKING_MISSED.remediation: Check the Ceph releases of the source's compute nodes and cluster for the fast-diff fixes (Ceph #61616: Pacific 16.2.14, Quincy 17.2.7, Reef 18.1.2); the disk scans in full for the rest of the migration.

DST_KEYPAIR_KEY_MISMATCH.remediation: Give the destination's migration user the source's key under that name: delete its keypair of that name and pre-stage keypairs, or create it again with the source's public key. A user of its own for each project credential keeps two tenants' keypairs of one name apart (Operations.md).

PROJECT_CREDENTIAL_EXPIRING.remediation: Have an admin write a new application credential for the project before this one expires - one that outlives the plan's cutover window, or never expires - (PUT /providers/{id}/projects/{project_id}/credentials), then check the provider: a step that runs after the expiry fails, a rollback included.

PROJECT_CREDENTIAL_UNRESTRICTED.remediation: Have an admin write a restricted application credential for the project in its place - Keystone creates one restricted unless asked otherwise - and delete the unrestricted one in Keystone: a restricted credential creates no application credential and no trust, so a stolen run directory gives no lasting access.

PROJECT_CREDENTIAL_ROLE_MISSING.remediation: Give the credential's user the role on the project in Keystone - member for the plan's steps, load-balancer_member for a plan that maps Octavia pools -, create a new application credential, which holds the roles its user has when it is created, and write it for the project; then check the provider and validate the plan again.
